decision.question: Should we launch a free plan?
decision.objective: Evaluate financial runway, acquisition velocity, infra strain, and cannibalization of launching a free tier.

findings.claim: With a current runway of 13.2 months and a cash balance of $1,650,000 against a net monthly burn of $125,000, launching an unmonetized or poorly guarded free plan risks depleting our gross margins (currently 0.74) through uncontrolled infrastructure and support cost explosions.

evidence.snippet: Current runway is 13.2 months, which is above the target minimum of 10.0 months but sensitive to margin compression.
Cash balance is $1,650,000 with a monthly net burn of $125,000.
Current gross margin stands at 0.74, which must be protected against cost explosions from free tiers.

limitations: Does not factor in macro demand shifts or degradation in organic traffic quality.
Assumes support and infrastructure scaling remain linear relative to active free users.

findings.claim: Launching a free plan can significantly accelerate top-of-funnel acquisition from our 65,000 monthly visitors, provided we manage infrastructure costs and cannibalization of existing paid trials.

evidence.snippet: Monthly visitors: 65,000; Trial signups: 1,100; Trial-to-paid conversion: 4.8%; New paid customers monthly: 53.

limitations: Does not account for viral loop coefficients or word-of-mouth amplifiers.
Assumes current web traffic acquisition quality remains stable.

findings.claim: Launching a free plan is feasible from an infrastructure standpoint only if strict usage ceilings and rate limits are enforced to contain marginal compute and storage costs per free user, currently estimated at $1.15.

evidence.snippet: Current monthly cloud cost is $14,500 with an estimated infra cost per free user of $1.15.

limitations: Does not account for sudden spikes in viral free signups that could overwhelm database multi-tenancy limits.
Assumes cloud provider pricing remains stable.

findings.claim: Launching an unrestricted free plan poses a severe threat to existing paid revenue and will overwhelm our high-touch support team with low-value inquiries, given our current capacity of 300 tickets per FTE.

evidence.snippet: Current support headcount is 4 FTE handling 1,200 monthly tickets at 300 tickets per FTE monthly.
Starter plan has 450 customers generating $35,550 MRR out of 655 total paying customers.

limitations: Does not account for potential top-of-funnel expansion via paid acquisition alternatives.
Assumes support ticket generation rates for free users mirror industry benchmarks.

findings.claim: Launching a free plan is viable only if strict usage caps and strategic feature gates are enforced to prevent paid cannibalization, given our strong base of 655 paying customers yielding solid MRR.

evidence.snippet: Current total paying customers stand at 655 across Starter, Pro, and Enterprise tiers.
Starter plan has 450 customers at $79/mo, representing the primary segment vulnerable to free tier cannibalization.

limitations: Requires robust instrumentation of usage ceilings to drive conversion.
Does not account for potential shifts in customer support scaling costs.

Under expected operating parameters, B usage caps generates an estimated $1,141,045.24 in cumulative 12-month net contribution while preserving 999.0 months of cash runway (safety threshold: 10.0 mo). The recommendation remains viable as long as free-to-paid conversion stays above 0.48%.

High Monte Carlo stability: 95.6% probability of top outcome with 99.8% runway solvency.

skeptic_challenges.challenge: The projected range of 1,000 to 10,000 free signups per month rests purely on unproven AI assumptions without telemetry grounding. Given 65,000 monthly visitors, assuming up to 15.3% of total top-of-funnel traffic converts into free signups ignores standard B2B conversion friction.
Growth assumes 1,500 to 10,000 free signups from 65,000 monthly visitors without historical precedent or channel breakdown. This represents an unproven extrapolation with no provenance verification.
Similar to Growth and CFO, Product relies on an unverified AI assumption (1,000 to 7,500 signups) with zero provenance. This overstates potential top-of-funnel capture.

Customer service projects a high cannibalization rate of 15% to 30%, citing general external research. However, with 450 Starter customers paying $79/mo, a 30% downgrade would catastrophically impact MRR by over $10k. Provenance must be proven against our specific tier overlap.
The 35% cost reduction from usage caps is an unproven AI assumption. Without hard telemetry on how users hit rate limits, this percentage is speculative.
The 12% base activation drop from gating lacks empirical backing. Strict gating could suppress conversion far below the projected base case.
